## 分诊 · `domain:engine` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts` ⇒ `domain:engine`.

Confirmed on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:02:25Z) — and the read turned up **a second site the card does not name**:

| site | code |
|---|---|
| `record-validator.ts:887` | `return parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? 'invalid value shape';` — inside `valueShapeViolation` (`:879`), the site the card reports |
| **`record-validator.ts:736`** | `const detail = parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? 'invalid value shape';` — **a second positional read of the same shape** |

⚠️ `:840`'s own comment already worries about exactly this: *"imports `valueShapeViolation`: two readings of these variables drifting by …"*. ⇒ **Both sites are in scope for this card.** A fix that changes only `:887` leaves the identical positional read at `:736` producing the identical wrong prescription, and the next measurement files this card again from the other door.

### Grade — p2

- **Not p3.** The failure lands on the **exact case `scan-value-shapes.ts`'s own header names as one the scan exists to find**, and it lands on the operator-facing prescription — the field whose documented contract is *"The first parse issue seen — the prescription an author acts on."* An operator running `os migrate value-shapes` over real legacy location data is told `expected number, received undefined` and left to derive a rename that **edit distance cannot reach** (`lat` ← `latitude`), which is precisely why `LocationValueSchema` declares the `aliases` map. The hint is built and then thrown away.
- **Not p1**, and the card is careful to say why: the value **is** flagged, the gate **does** stay shut. Nothing bad merges or migrates. The defect is in the quality of the diagnosis, not in the verdict.

⭐ The asymmetry is what makes this worth a card rather than a nit: the **identically-shaped `address` case gets the full prescription** (`postal_code` → `postalCode`, with the alias hint), and the reason is invisible from inside — `address` declares every member optional so no `invalid_type` can sort ahead of the `unrecognized_keys` issue, while `location` requires the `lat`/`lng` pair so **two always do**. That means the diagnosis quality of this scan depends on an unrelated property of each schema (whether its members happen to be optional), which nobody chose and nobody can see.

### Boundary test — Bug, no manual floor

Preferring the `unrecognized_keys` issue over positional `issues[0]` changes only the **text** of an existing finding. No accept set moves, no value newly passes or fails, no gate changes verdict. Ordinary lane work.

### ⛔ The fence the card puts on its own suggestion — adopted, and it is the real work

> Worth confirming that the same positional read does not mislead **the other structured-JSON classes** before changing it.

That is deliverable 1, and it is now bigger than the card thought, because there are two call sites. ⇒ Enumerate the structured-JSON value classes, and for each ask whether an `unrecognized_keys` issue can co-occur with an `invalid_type` one. `location` and `address` are the two measured; the rest are unmeasured. ⛔ Do not ship "prefer `unrecognized_keys`" as a blanket rule until that sweep exists — a class where the unrecognized key is genuinely the *less* actionable diagnosis would be made worse by it.

### ⭐ Why no gate caught it, and what the fix owes

The card's diagnosis here is the sharpest part and it prescribes its own pin:

- `scan-value-shapes.test.ts` uses **this exact value** (`{ geo: { latitude: 1, longitude: 2 } }`) and asserts only `report.blocking === 1` — **never `detail`**.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.test.ts:313` **does** assert the rename text, and reaches it by **searching the issue list** for the `unrecognized_keys` issue rather than reading `issues[0]`.

⇒ The spec layer already knows the ordering is not meaningful; the consumer that formats the operator's report does not. **The pin belongs in `scan-value-shapes.test.ts`, asserting `detail`** — the fixture is already there and already carries the right value; only the assertion is missing. ⛔ A fix that lands without that assertion leaves the case pinned in a way that cannot see this defect, which is the family this shift has been cataloguing.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

⚠️⚠️ **DELIVERABLE 1 IS A SWEEP, AND IT COMES FIRST.** The card fences its own suggestion and triage adopted the fence: *"Worth confirming that the same positional read does not mislead the other structured-JSON classes before changing it."* ⇒ **Enumerate the structured-JSON value classes, and for each ask whether an `unrecognized_keys` issue can co-occur with an `invalid_type` one.** Only `location` and `address` are measured; the rest are unmeasured. ⛔ **Do NOT ship "prefer `unrecognized_keys`" as a blanket rule until that sweep exists** — a class where the unrecognized key is genuinely the *less* actionable diagnosis would be made **worse** by it.

**The pin is already half-written — ⛔ do not ship without finishing it.** `packages/objectql/src/validation/scan-value-shapes.test.ts` uses **this exact value** (`{ geo: { latitude: 1, longitude: 2 } }`) and asserts only `report.blocking === 1` — **never `detail`**. ⇒ **The fixture is there and already carries the right value; only the assertion is missing.** ⛔ A fix that lands without asserting `detail` leaves the case pinned in a way that **cannot see this defect** — the exact family this shift has been cataloguing.

Read it before designing yours.

**Grade p2, and why not p1** (the card is careful and triage adopted it): the value **is** flagged and the gate **does** stay shut — nothing bad merges or migrates. ⛔ The defect is in the **quality of the diagnosis**, not in the verdict. ⛔ Do not widen this into a verdict change.

⚠️ **Anchors** (card's at `a06faebbe4`, triage's at `f1d7872` — ⛔ re-derive, files move daily): `record-validator.ts:736`, `:840`, `:879`, `:887`; `scan-value-shapes.test.ts`; `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.test.ts:313`.

⭐ **Reproduce end-to-end through the real exported scan**, as the card did — `scanValueShapes` with (A) the legacy `{latitude,longitude}`, (B) the `{postal_code}` address case as the contrast that already works, (C) an all-clean control that must report `blocking=0`. **Three cases, two of them controls.**

**Clause-② reading (this seat's, not binding)**: `no` — you change only the **text** of an existing finding. No accept set moves, no value newly passes or fails, no gate changes verdict. ⭐ Re-derive with the `dist/index.d.ts` ablation on `@objectstack/objectql` and state both limbs separately.

⚠️ **This `Clause-②` reading is this seat's and is NOT binding on you.** Re-derive it from your own diff and re-declare it in your report. This seat got a tier call wrong in BOTH directions today (#14552 predicted a park that measurement retired; #14646 and #14935 declared `no` for diffs that widened a published surface) — every one was caught only because the round re-measured.

⚠️ **Instrument limit, stated because two rounds burned time on it**: `api-surface/` artifacts exist **only for `packages/spec`**. For any other package the published surface is its `files[]` + `types` (`dist/**`). The instrument that works: build at your head → swap the changed source file back to `origin/main` → rebuild → diff the built `dist/index.d.ts` → restore **byte-exact** and prove the restore (blob == HEAD blob AND `git diff HEAD` empty). The test is 「**does any exported symbol/signature move, or is any request newly accepted or rejected**」 — ⛔ not 「did the signature line change」.

✅ **The Corepack CI defect is FIXED.** `check-regen-pending.mjs --self-test` reddened `origin/main`'s own push build and six PRs today; PR #16002 landed as `f50c394da` (verified by content on `origin/main`). If you cut from current `main` you will not see it. If you DO see `Lint & Repo Gates` red on `check:merge-driver` with `✗ self-test failed -- 1 failure(s) (cases and floor)`, your base predates `f50c394da` — merge `main` and re-run. ⛔ Do not skip, disable or quarantine anything over it.

⭐ **Discipline notes earned the hard way today, all from real failures:**
1. **An ablation whose restore outruns its measurement produces a confident WRONG green.** A round hit exactly that — its mutating helper's own `EXIT` trap restored the file as it exited, and the suite then passed against the *restored* tree. Prove the mutation is on disk **before** measuring (anchored grep counts, or `git hash-object` != HEAD blob) and prove the restore **after**, **in one shell**.
2. **A failure count is not a reading about success while anything is still running.** Read `status` explicitly. This seat published a false 「the re-run cleared it」 today by counting only completed-and-failed.
3. **A zero symbol count needs its comment filter run FIRST** — code that *documents* an absence makes a bare count non-zero — and **every zero-hit grep needs a firing positive control**. A control aimed at a symbol that does not exist in the repo is not a control.
4. **`cancelled` is not `failed`.** On a PR whose head just moved, 「N lanes cancelled」 in the OLD head's run is `lint.yml`'s `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`, not evidence about that head. Read the RUN-level conclusion plus job timestamps against the new run's `created_at`.
5. **The shared verify lock is contended.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` returning **exit 99 is a timeout = NO READING**, ⛔ not a green and ⛔ not a red. Re-run to a real result and say so. Multiple rounds recorded 99s today (540s / 352s / 459s waits) with the holder alive and building normally — that is cost, not breakage.
6. **Shared-ref hazard**: `origin/main` moves under you when a sibling worktree fetches. Pin every diff and merge to a **sha**, never to the ref name. One round read 9 changed files that were really 5.

⛔ **Never edit `content/docs/releases/**`** in a code PR — release notes are written centrally at release time. Your PR's input to them is its **changeset**. E3 (2026-09-05) 「已发布必修，其余立卡」 — "published" is a MEASUREMENT against built `dist/**/*.d.ts`, `dist/**/*.{js,mjs,cjs}` and `content/docs/**`, not a guess.

⛔ **Worktree-first** (one dedicated worktree, this repo AND any sibling you touch) and ⛔ **never `git stash`** — `refs/stash` lives in the common `.git` dir, so all worktrees share one LIFO stack and your `pop` takes another agent's entry while reporting success. Use a patch file or a wip commit. ⛔ Never force-push or rebase a pushed branch.

**Bump level**: additive widening of a published surface ⇒ at least `minor`. ⭐ **The act wins over the commit type** — the gate at `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` only refuses `major`, so it will not catch a `patch` that should have been `minor`.

## ⚠️ Correction — this seat's Zone 2.1 was FALSE in its second limb, and the round measured it

PM dispatch seat, `session_01ARYe3yQTQCUFm5qPYNgKaJ`. Correcting my own dispatch brief, because the claim was load-bearing: it said which classes could exhibit the defect, and it was wrong in the direction that **understates** the defect.

### What I asserted, and what is true

My brief (echoing the card and triage) explained the `location`-vs-`address` asymmetry like this:

> `address` declares **every member optional** so no `invalid_type` can sort ahead of `unrecognized_keys`; `location` **requires** `lat`/`lng` so **two always do**.

**The first half is right, the second is false.** All-optional members rule out a **missing**-member type error — `{}` parses green — but a **wrong-typed declared member still emits one**. Measured by the round:

```
{ street: 5, postal_code: '98101' }
  -> issues: [ invalid_type(street), unrecognized_keys ]
  -> reported detail: "Invalid input: expected string, received number"
```

⇒ ⭐ **The defect was never `location`-only.** The card's contrast case (B, `{postal_code}`) appears to work **only because its fixture carries no type error** — not because `address` is structurally immune. Change the fixture and `address` fails the same way. That case is now pinned too.

### Why this mattered rather than being a footnote

The brief used "address is structurally immune" as the *explanation* of the asymmetry, and an explanation that is wrong in that direction makes the blast radius look smaller than it is. ⛔ A round that had adopted my framing would have pinned `location` and left `address` un-pinned on the reasoning that it could not regress.

⭐ It did not, because the brief also said the sweep was **deliverable 1 and came first**, and the sweep is what caught it. That ordering is the only reason this is cheap.

### The sweep's result, which discharges the card's fence properly

Of the **16** classes the two readers cover, only **`location` and `address`** are backed by a key-closed object schema, so only they can emit `unrecognized_keys` **at all** — the preference is a **literal no-op** for the other 14, and both classes it reaches curate an `aliases` map. ⇒ The card's fence (*"confirm the same positional read does not mislead the other structured-JSON classes"*) is discharged by measurement rather than by assertion, and the "blanket rule" risk it warned about does not exist here.

### Also endorsed for the record

⭐ The round reported an **ablation script bug** rather than silently re-running it: its first attempt returned exit 1 on *every* leg including the green one — the zero-match trap, repo-root-relative paths handed to a `--filter`ed vitest that runs in the package dir, so "No test files found". Its restore held byte-exact and it said so. ⚠️ That is the same family as this seat's own errors today (a probe that measures nothing looks exactly like a finding), and naming it is what makes the second reading trustworthy.

⭐ And it fixed **three doc contracts** that still said "the first parse issue" (`ValueShapeFinding.detail`, `valueShapeViolation`'s return contract, `AdmittedValueShapeViolation.detail`) — the last fed by the same variable as site 1. ⛔ Leaving those would have left the code correct and its own documentation falsified.
